notes: openIMIS is an open-source health-insurance management system; this is its FHIR R4 API, served by the openimis-be-api_fhir_r4_py module at <host>/api/api_fhir_r4. No machine spec could be captured: the module does mount drf-spectacular at /api/api_fhir_r4/docs/, but that endpoint returns HTTP 500 on the public demo even with a valid token, so the spec was authored from the module's own DRF router (api_fhir_r4/urls.py), its viewset classes, and live introspection of demo.openimis.org — the API root listing, an HTTP OPTIONS probe of every collection and instance route for the exact allowed methods, and a GET of every resource for the field sets. 'Full' here means every route the router registers: 19 FHIR resource types (Patient, Group, Claim, ClaimResponse, Contract, Coverage, CoverageEligibilityRequest, Location, Organization, Practitioner, PractitionerRole, Medication, ActivityDefinition, InsurancePlan, Communication, CommunicationRequest, Invoice, PaymentNotice, Subscription), 13 CodeSystem lookups, 2 ValueSet pricelists and login — 56 paths / 136 operations, against 29 GET-only operations in the previous copy. The previous copy also carried HealthcareService and Condition, which the current module does not register; they were removed (health facilities are Organization/Location and diagnoses are CodeSystem/diagnosis). Resource schemas are element sets observed on the demo instance rather than the full HL7 FHIR R4 element set, so a field the demo data never populates may be missing; no example values are carried because the demo database holds person-level data. Communication, Invoice, PaymentNotice, Subscription, CoverageEligibilityRequest and the two ValueSet pricelists returned no instances (or 500) on the demo, so those schemas are minimal and marked as such in their descriptions. Which endpoints a given deployment exposes depends on which openIMIS modules are installed — urls.py registers Patient/Group only when the insuree module is present, Claim only with the claim module, and so on. openIMIS also ships a separate SPDCI Registry Core API (openimis-be-api_dci_py, which does publish an OpenAPI file) and a GraphQL API; neither is reachable through this adaptor and neither is modelled here.
